text: The 'deviant (wayward) causal chain' problem, illustrated by Davidson's nervous climber, shows that:
choices: Reasons are never causes of action
A belief-desire pair can cause the very movement it rationalizes, yet the result still fails to be an intentional action
There are no genuinely basic actions
explanation: The deviant-causal-chain problem (Davidson's climber, so unnerved by the thought of loosening his grip that his hand trembles and he lets go) shows that a belief-desire pair can cause the very movement it rationalizes without the result being an intentional action - so 'caused by reasons' needs a 'right kind of causation' clause. Option 0 abandons the causal theory entirely, and options 2 and 3 are unrelated over-generalizations.
